package_info.why_malicious: These packages are copycats of the legitimate 'mitmproxy' library but have had critical security safeguards removed, introducing an artificial remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability. This allows anyone on the same network to execute arbitrary code on the host running the web interface, representing a severe security risk.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when mitmproxy web interface is started)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Removes critical HTTP security headers and adds permissive CORS headers, allowing any origin to access the API and all HTTP methods to be used.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security headers and enabling permissive CORS is a classic way to expose internal APIs to external attackers, especially in a tool that exposes a web interface for controlling a proxy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to restrict access to the web API using headers like X-Frame-Options and to limit CORS to trusted origins. The malicious version removes these protections, making the API accessible to anyone on the network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Permissive CORS headers may be used in development environments for testing, but never in production or security-sensitive tools.
key_indicators: Addition of Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST, GET, DELETE, OPTIONS

attack_chain.action: User installs and runs the malicious mitmproxy2 or mitmproxy-iframe package, believing it to be a legitimate or newer version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Web interface is started with insecure configuration.

attack_chain.action: Web interface exposes HTTP API with all security safeguards removed.
attack_chain.leads_to: API is accessible to anyone on the same network.

attack_chain.action: Attacker on the same network sends crafted HTTP requests to the exposed API, triggering remote code execution on the victim's machine.

behavioral_signatures: mitmproxy web interface running with CORS headers set to '*'
Absence of X-Frame-Options and other standard security headers in HTTP responses from mitmproxy web interface
Unexpected exposure of mitmproxy API to non-localhost network interfaces
file_indicators: mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py with commented out or missing X-Frame-Options header
Presence of Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * in mitmproxy web interface code
network_indicators: mitmproxy web interface accessible from non-localhost addresses
Unusual HTTP requests to mitmproxy API endpoints from other devices on the same network
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installations of 'mitmproxy2' or 'mitmproxy-iframe' packages. Inspect mitmproxy web interface HTTP responses for missing security headers and permissive CORS settings. Alert if the web interface is accessible from non-localhost addresses or if API endpoints are accessed by unexpected clients. Review package source code for removal of security headers and addition of wildcard CORS headers.
